attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The Yang-Mills boundary OPE for reflected Wilson triples has not been computed in the locked algebra, so B, N, and the leading quotient kernel H are not yet known to exist with the required uniform collar limits.
steps: Fix a finite locked Wilson collar family F_i^\delta and form N^\delta_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i^\delta,F_j^\delta).
Regulated reflection positivity gives N^\delta\ge0; fixed-collar RG convergence transfers this to N\ge0 by closedness of the finite OS cone.
Assume diagonal trace continuity, so any positive additive contact with zero diagonal vanishes by Cauchy-Schwarz; remaining boundary effect is tested as N=B\circ M.
Since diagonal congruence is same-theory harmless, normalize N, B, and M. Then \widehat M=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B=q, so intended OS positivity on this block is exactly q\ge0.
For three Wilson hairpins, compute det q explicitly; the quotient phase holonomy \arg(q_{12}q_{23}\overline{q_{13}}) enters at the first phase-sensitive minor.

For a differentiable quotient q(\lambda)=\mathbf1\mathbf1^*+\lambda H+o(\lambda), zero-sum test vectors annihilate the rank-one part, so positivity for small \lambda forces H to be PSD on the zero-sum subspace.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite matrix argument is valid, but it proves only a conditional bridge. A full proof still needs RG domination of reflected collar probes, no additive boundary defect, nonzero multiplicative B entries, and PSD of q for every realized finite Wilson block.

assumptions: For each fixed collar, regulated reflection positivity and RG convergence give a valid PSD limit matrix N.
Diagonal Wilson trace limits exist with positive diagonal entries, and positive additive boundary contacts have been eliminated or proved zero.
The boundary OPE is multiplicative on the finite block: N_{ij}=B_{ij}M_{ij}, with B Hermitian, B_{ii}>0, and B_{ij}\ne0 on the tested block.
The finite family belongs to the locked gauge-invariant test algebra before and after collar collapse.
definitions: source object: a finite locked gauge-invariant Wilson collar family F_i^\delta supported in t>\delta, its reflected collar-limit OS matrix N, and the multiplicative boundary Gram factor B from reflected Wilson hairpin OPE.
target object: the intended continuum OS matrix M_{ij}=S(\Theta F_i,F_j) on the same Wilson observables, hence the pre-Hilbert OS form before null quotient.
controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions through convergence of finite reflected quadratic forms plus a collar trace limit.

same-theory condition: collar collapse may change observables only by diagonal/unitary congruence already present in the locked renormalization; any pair-dependent boundary factor must be divided out without adding boundary observables.

equations.label: multiplicative boundary factor
equations.valid_when: The reflected Wilson collar OPE has no surviving additive contact and its pair-dependent part is a multiplicative boundary factor.

equations.label: normalized Schur preimage
equations.valid_when: All tested diagonal entries are positive and diagonal congruences are regarded as same-theory normalizations.

equations.label: three-hairpin determinant
equations.valid_when: q is a normalized Hermitian 3-by-3 quotient matrix with q_{ij}=r_{ij}e^{i\phi_{ij}}.

equations.label: infinitesimal quotient test
equations.latex: q(\lambda)=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^*+\lambda H+o(\lambda),\quad q(\lambda)\ge0\ (0<\lambda\ll1)\Rightarrow c^*Hc\ge0\ \forall c:\sum_i c_i=0
equations.valid_when: A physical or auxiliary parameter \lambda gives a differentiable family of realized quotient blocks with q(0) the rank-one all-ones matrix.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A falsifier is a realized Wilson triple with the determinant above negative, or an infinitesimal boundary OPE kernel H with c^*Hc<0 for some zero-sum vector c.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the exact finite-dimensional bridge between collar-limit reflection positivity and same-theory OS positivity after Wilson boundary collapse; it replaces vague anomaly language by a PSD quotient test.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite Wilson collar collapse preserves same-theory OS positivity exactly when the normalized Schur preimage q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B is positive semidefinite on every realized locked Wilson block.

assumptions: A valid parameter t exists; it is not merely a formal coupling expansion unless the Wilson OPE proves Hadamard multiplicativity.
All q_t are normalized Schur quotients of realized locked Wilson collar blocks.
The branch does not assume this semigroup structure for Yang-Mills; it is a possible certificate only.
definitions: Hadamard semigroup: normalized kernels q_t on a fixed finite Wilson block satisfying q_0=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^*, q_{s+t}=q_s\circ q_t, and entrywise continuity in t.
logarithmic quotient generator: a Hermitian matrix h with q_t=e^{t h} entrywise and h_{ii}=0.
conditionally positive generator: \sum_{ij}\overline c_i c_j h_{ij}\ge0 for every c with \sum_i c_i=0.

equations.label: semigroup representation
equations.valid_when: The boundary quotient OPE exponentiates additively in the parameter t on the same finite Wilson block.

equations.label: Schoenberg certificate
equations.latex: q_t\ge0\ \forall t\ge0\Longleftrightarrow\sum_{ij}\overline c_i c_j h_{ij}\ge0\ \forall c:\sum_i c_i=0
equations.valid_when: The finite normalized kernels form a continuous nonvanishing Hermitian Hadamard semigroup.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If no physical Hadamard semigroup is produced, log-CPD is only a sufficient heuristic; the valid falsifier remains a finite negative principal minor of q.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma explains precisely when log-CND/CPD arguments are valid rather than an overclaim.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the Wilson quotient kernels form a continuous Hadamard semigroup, then the finite PSD quotient test can be promoted to a generator test: the logarithmic boundary quotient must be conditionally positive on zero-sum vectors, and this condition is sufficient for all finite blocks.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a realized Wilson triple or infinitesimal quotient kernel gives a negative principal minor, proving the same-theory OS bridge fails.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if the boundary OPE proves q\ge0 for all finite locked Wilson blocks, or proves a valid Hadamard semigroup with conditionally positive logarithmic generator.
control_decision.reason: The branch is no longer repeating topology closure; it has a sharp finite matrix obstruction and a calculable boundary OPE target.

dependency_updates.description: The formal closed-cone step now stops at N\ge0 for collar-limit matrices; the same-theory step is the separate quotient condition q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\ge0.
The algebra must contain the Wilson collar triples used to test quotient determinants and must not absorb pair-dependent boundary factors as new observables.
Topology must give convergence not only of fixed reflected forms but also of the collar trace limits defining N and the boundary OPE factor B.
Compute B, N, and the leading quotient kernel H for reflected Wilson hairpin triples; this is the current decisive analytic task.

falsifiers: A realized reflected Wilson triple with 1+2r12 r23 r13 cos(Phi)-r12^2-r23^2-r13^2<0 is a direct same-theory falsifier.
A leading boundary quotient kernel H with a zero-sum vector c satisfying c^*Hc<0 falsifies any valid small-parameter Schur-preimage passage.
A boundary factor B_{ij}=0 while N_{ij}\ne0 makes the quotient singular and signals that the collar algebra is not the same theory.
A proof that positivity survives only by retaining the dressed matrix N=B\circ M, instead of the intended M, shows that a new boundary theory has been introduced.
An indefinite additive contact term at the reflection plane invalidates the reduction to a multiplicative Schur quotient.
The cutoff-removal topology might control fixed collars but fail to control the simultaneous reflected Wilson collar collapse.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 212 converts the Wilson boundary obstruction into an exact finite Schur-preimage bridge plus a perturbative tangent detector. The valid criterion remains q=\widehat N\oslash\widehat B\ge0 on realized Wilson blocks; log-CND/CPD is justified only if a Hadamard semigroup is proved. The first concrete falsifier is now either a negative three-hairpin quotient determinant or a zero-sum negative leading quotient kernel from the boundary OPE.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Compute the leading boundary quotient H for three mirror-smooth Wilson hairpins with a common reflection-plane footprint; evaluate the determinant formula and the zero-sum quadratic forms before attempting any higher-minor theorem.
